question: Find the value of $x$ satisfying $\begin{vmatrix}x&2&1\\1&x&2\\2&1&x\end{vmatrix}=0$, given that $x$ is an integer greater than $1$.
explanation:
Step 1: Expand the determinant
Expanding along the first row, $$x(x^2-2)-2(x-4)+(1-2x)=0$$
Step 2: Simplify
This gives $$x^3-2x-2x+8+1-2x=0$$ or $$x^3-6x+9=0$$
Step 3: Factorise the expression
Since $x=-3$ is a root, $$x^3-6x+9=(x+3)(x^2-3x+3)$$
Step 4: Analyse the roots
The quadratic factor has discriminant $9-12=-3$, so it has no real roots. The only real value is $x=-3$.
Step 5: Apply the stated condition
Since $-3$ is not greater than $1$, there is no integer $x>1$ satisfying the determinant equation.

options.A: There is no integer $x>1$ satisfying the equation.
